title_candidates: Claude is adding machine-readable marks to new model output
summary: New Claude models add hidden marks to generated text and signed provenance to supported files, but those signals do not prove authorship or accuracy.

primary_source.title: How Claude marks AI-generated content
primary_source.author: Anthropic
key_facts: Claude models launched on or after August 2 support machine-readable marking from launch.
Generated text from supported models carries an embedded watermark, while supported files can carry signed C2PA metadata.
The marks apply across Claude products and supported cloud deployments worldwide.
Anthropic has not yet released public detection instructions.
A detected mark can indicate processing by Claude but does not prove original authorship, accuracy, or lack of later editing.
Heavy text editing can weaken detection, while screenshots and file conversion can strip provenance metadata.

supporting_sources.title: C2PA
key_facts: C2PA is an open standard for recording signed information about the origin and editing history of digital content.

prerequisites: A document or file you created with Claude
Access to its original chat or project notes

steps.instruction: Record how Claude assisted, preserve the original file and source notes, and add an accurate visible disclosure when authorship matters.
Wait for an official Anthropic detection mechanism and treat either a positive or negative result as limited evidence.

references.title: C2PA
references.author: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity

risk_flags: Public detection instructions are not available yet, so the guide must not promise a working detector.
A mark indicates possible Claude processing and must not be presented as proof of authorship, plagiarism, or accuracy.
